extracted.intended_audience: college mathematics instructors, especially new instructors and meeting leaders for faculty development
extracted.subtask_short: faculty meeting on classroom control and proctoring
extracted.subtask_description: Designing and running a short faculty-development meeting/workshop for instructors addressing classroom control in interactive mathematics classes and proctoring tests/examinations, including preparation, agenda, materials, suggested facilitation phases, and concrete classroom/proctoring practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide an analytical framework for classroom difficulties
rubrics_metrics.description: To provide participants with an analytical framework for categorizing, and perhaps beginning to understand and put into perspective, the difficulties that they may have experienced in their classroom.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the meeting to give instructors a way to analyze control challenges so they can better understand and respond to them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage sharing of uncomfortable classroom experiences
rubrics_metrics.description: To have participants share classroom experiences that make them feel uncomfortable. Many meeting participants may not normally be able to speak about these issues with colleagues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create a safe, confidential tone so instructors can candidly describe loss-of-control situations they have faced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Normalize that others face control/power issues
rubrics_metrics.description: To have participants realize that others also face serious issues of control in their classes, and that they are not alone in their experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use peer sharing and examples to reduce feelings of isolation and discourage assuming one is uniquely failing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Help instructors find workable solutions
rubrics_metrics.description: To have instructors think about the challenges that they and their colleagues face, and find workable solutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus discussion on practical, implementable strategies rather than abstract blame or idealized approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alert instructors to potential control problems
rubrics_metrics.description: To alert instructors who have not experienced serious issues of control and power that such problems can occur, and what the nature of the problems can be.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide concrete examples and scenarios so instructors who haven't experienced problems can recognize them early.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide time for reflection and planning next steps
rubrics_metrics.description: To give participants a chance to reflect on their experiences, and to give them an opportunity to think about what they could do differently next time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include exercises or prompts that lead participants to identify specific changes they will try in upcoming classes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meeting leader familiar with participant issues and interactive-class nature
rubrics_metrics.description: The meeting leader needs to be familiar both with the (1) kinds of issues that participants are facing in their classes—and how they have responded to these issues—and (2) what about the nature of an interactive classroom can contribute to the difficult situations that instructors face.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leader preparation should include knowing common interactive-class dynamics (e.g., off-topic conversations, pacing issues) and prior instructor responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Find out participants' control issues in advance
rubrics_metrics.description: The meeting leader needs to find out what kinds of control issues the participants have been dealing with in their classes through interviews or a survey.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use interviews, surveys, or classroom visits (if available) to tailor the meeting to participants' real concerns and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tone-setting via pre-circulated 'difficult situations' sheet
rubrics_metrics.description: If the meeting is to be one where the leader candidly expects people to share their experiences of losing control of their class, the leader may have to do some tone-setting work beforehand (e.g., write up a sheet describing some difficult situations and distribute it to participants).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct situation descriptions that participants recognize but that are not so pointed as to make them feel overexposed; consider distributing prior to meeting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invite experienced instructors who recovered control
rubrics_metrics.description: If it seems appropriate, the meeting leader could invite experienced instructors who have dealt with control issues in their own classes to attend the meeting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ask speakers to emphasize practical recovery strategies; avoid framing as 'what you did wrong'—focus on pragmatic steps and hope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research literature and synthesize handout on strategies
rubrics_metrics.description: The meeting leader may research some of the literature dealing with assertiveness, classroom behavior and teaching strategies, in order to synthesize a handout that relates some strategies for dealing with behavioral problems in general, or specific issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide curated references (e.g., McKeachie, Cangelosi, Rinne) and synthesize actionable strategies into a concise handout for participants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan to end meeting on a positive note
rubrics_metrics.description: Plan to end the meeting on a positive note; it may be helpful to consider exactly how to do this as part of preparation (e.g., make a summary of things going well).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider techniques like summarizing successes, emphasizing solutions over problems, and sincere affirmations; avoid superficial praise that may seem insincere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan ground rules ahead of time
rubrics_metrics.description: If you plan to enforce any ground rules at the meeting, then plan them beforehand. Ground rules may be circulated before the meeting or handed out and described at the beginning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be explicit about confidentiality and respectful listening; circulate or post ground rules to set tone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare sufficient copies of meeting materials and handouts
rubrics_metrics.description: Make sufficient copies of meeting materials that you think may be helpful to the participants (e.g., 'Control in the Classroom' handout).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure all participants receive materials; include reference lists and sample classroom situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discuss problems specific to interactive classrooms
rubrics_metrics.description: Agenda item: A discussion of problems that can arise with management of the interactive classroom (focus on problems due to the nature of interactive classes—off-topic conversations, mismatch between group work and other activities, slowed pace, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize structural causes of problems (format and activities) rather than solely blaming individuals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide opportunity for participants to describe their classroom situations
rubrics_metrics.description: Agenda item: Discussion with others of how you see your classroom situation, and what you feel you would like to see happen differently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allocate time for each participant to talk and receive peer support, ideas, and advice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on immediate actionable possibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Agenda item: What can be done now? What possibilities does the current situation present?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage participants to identify concrete actions they can try in the next class session.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discuss prior classroom management strategies and outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Agenda item: Discussion of some classroom management strategies that people have tried in the past, and the results that they have seen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Share both successful and unsuccessful examples to inform realistic expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reflect on preventing recurrence of issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Agenda item: What can we learn from this? How can we conduct ourselves so that we don’t have to go through this kind of an experience again and again and again?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage planning of systemic classroom design changes and instructor habits to reduce repeated problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set explicit meeting phases rather than rigid schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: Run the meeting in loose, chronological phases—set ground rules, tone-setting, mini-lecture, sharing, strategy formulation, wrap-up—rather than a rigid minute-by-minute agenda.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow flexibility to follow participant concerns while ensuring core phases are covered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set and use ground rules during meeting
rubrics_metrics.description: Set ground rules, if ground rules are explicitly mentioned and used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use ground rules to protect confidentiality and create a respectful environment for candid sharing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead a tone-setting exercise (e.g., Student Situations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Lead a tone-setting exercise such as the 'Student Situations' sheet: ask participants to review and discuss with a neighbor before broader discussion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Small-pair discussion helps participants ease into candid group conversations; expand to group when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Give a short mini-lecture on typical interactive-class problems
rubrics_metrics.description: Give a short 'mini-lecture' on typical problems that seem to arise from interactive classrooms, and list ideas for addressing these problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize differences between problems arising from interactive formats versus individual student issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use active listening and sensitive facilitation for sharing
rubrics_metrics.description: Invite participants to share their experiences, and for other participants to support them. Use active listening and sensitive facilitation to draw out experiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Facilitator should model supportive responses and manage emotional dynamics to keep discussion productive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formulate concrete strategies and distribute handouts
rubrics_metrics.description: Formulate concrete strategies and ideas for individual participants to try out when they go back to their classes. Pass out copies of the handout 'Control in the Classroom' or similar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure strategies are specific, actionable, and linked to participant-identified problems; include follow-up suggestions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wrap up on an upbeat, sincere note emphasizing positives
rubrics_metrics.description: Wrap up the meeting on an upbeat note, trying to sincerely emphasize that there are positive things going on in the participants’ classrooms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize solutions and successes rather than dwelling solely on problems; use sincere, not perfunctory, praise (avoid cheap ploys).

rubrics_metrics.name: Have participants evaluate the workshop
rubrics_metrics.description: Have the participants evaluate the workshop.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect feedback to improve future meetings and to check whether participants feel supported and prepared.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use voluntary, non-judgmental invitation to expedite attendance
rubrics_metrics.description: Instead of holding a mandatory meeting, circulate an invitation asking people to attend if they would like to; the tone should be inviting and deliberately non-judgmental.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize informality and learning rather than confession or failure; include clear objectives in the invitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide meeting materials and literature-based handouts
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare copies of the handout 'Control in the Classroom,' other handouts developed from the literature on classroom management, and references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include sample classroom-control situations and curated readings to support follow-up learning.

rubrics_metrics.name: When starting group exercises, organize groups physically and by count-off
rubrics_metrics.description: When starting a group exercise, count the students off and have them physically move to a designated area of the classroom to meet their team.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Physical movement helps form intended groups rather than letting existing homework groups form spontaneously.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipate off-task work during group activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Be aware that if students work in their homework groups during class time, they may work on homework assignments rather than the learning activities assigned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan for this possibility by clarifying goals and monitoring groups; design activities that differ from homework tasks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan for groups working at different paces
rubrics_metrics.description: Groups may work at different paces; if some consistently finish early, plan additional exercises for quick students.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare extension tasks or challenges to keep fast groups engaged without interrupting others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Closely monitor student activity during group exercises
rubrics_metrics.description: During a group exercise, closely monitor students’ activity and be on the look-out for students who seem to be talking about things other than the assigned learning activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Circulate actively and intervene early when groups appear off-task.

rubrics_metrics.name: If groups are off-task, ask about their progress and redirect
rubrics_metrics.description: If it becomes clear that students are not working on the assigned learning activity, ask where they are in the problem; if they have finished, ask them to explain their work to others or write it on the board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use gentle, specific prompts to refocus and get evidence of engagement rather than confrontational admonitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: At end of group exercise, loudly request attention and persist
rubrics_metrics.description: When ending a group exercise go to the front of the room, and loudly ask for everybody’s attention. Repeat the request until the talking stops.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Persist until silence is achieved; combine with other techniques (see below) if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge student contributions when class is noisy
rubrics_metrics.description: When a student answers a question and others are talking, thank the student and ask the class to hear the contribution; once talking stops, ask the student to repeat their answer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publicly value contributions to discourage disregard; if talking persists, employ additional strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use a menu of attention-regaining strategies
rubrics_metrics.description: If talking does not stop, consider: telling the class the next point is critical (or writing it on the board); waiting obviously for talking to stop before making a point; trying 'speak–write–speak' (state point, write summary, restate); directly asking the disruptive student by name a question about the point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware these methods carry risk (e.g., appearing foolish if students ignore you); choose according to context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use instructor silence selectively to maintain order
rubrics_metrics.description: Some instructors are able to employ silence as a means to maintain order, particularly during instructor-centered portions of the lesson.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Silence can be effective where instructor voice is the norm; less effective during active student work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set and stick to ground rules for acceptable classroom activity
rubrics_metrics.description: Set ground rules—and stick to them—for what kinds of activity are acceptable during class.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make expectations explicit at the start of activities and apply them consistently to build norms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain goals of group activity at start to frame engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: At the beginning of a group activity, take a minute to explain the goals of the activity with emphasis on what students will know or be able to do as a result of participating.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clear goals reduce drift to unrelated tasks (e.g., homework).

rubrics_metrics.name: Occasionally require groups to present work publicly
rubrics_metrics.description: Occasionally ask all of the groups to go and work the activity on the board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public presentation increases accountability and provides models for other groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: If group not working, ask for status and insist on engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: If you spot a student or group who is not working on the activity you have assigned, ask how much they have completed; if 'not much', suggest they get to work and repeat as necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use repeated, varied prompts to redirect rather than public shaming.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form groups and scaffold the start to encourage interaction
rubrics_metrics.description: Form the students into groups yourself at the beginning of the activity, and if students are new to group work, ask them to begin by introducing themselves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit formation reduces inertia and encourages interpersonal engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribute one worksheet per group and appoint a reader
rubrics_metrics.description: Distribute only one copy of the worksheet to each group, and appoint someone in the group to read it to the others at the beginning of the activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shared materials and roles encourage collaboration rather than solitary work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arrange seating to promote face-to-face interaction
rubrics_metrics.description: Try to arrive before students and, if possible, rearrange chairs so students will be facing each other when they take their seats.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Physical arrangement influences interaction patterns; set up seating for collaboration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge student struggle and offer follow-up support
rubrics_metrics.description: Remember that struggling students are often trying to understand; suggest meeting after class or during office hours to discuss points in detail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offer targeted follow-up to help students without slowing whole-class pace; encourage incremental understanding during class.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage significant out-of-class study time to keep pace
rubrics_metrics.description: Remind students that they should also be spending quite a lot of time outside of class working to understand the material (some prescriptions suggest two hours outside class for every hour in class).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set reasonable expectations for outside study and provide guidance for productive study habits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevent dominance by directing questions and calling equitably
rubrics_metrics.description: Direct some questions to particular students as well as leaving some open to volunteers; make an effort to call on all students equally, possibly in a pattern (e.g., every other seat).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance participation to avoid repeated dominance by a few students; respect student preferences not to be called on.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultivate an environment valuing genuine attempts
rubrics_metrics.description: Make the classroom an environment where genuine attempts to get to grips with and think about problems are valued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Praise effortful reasoning and normalize partial answers as part of learning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect students' wishes about being called on
rubrics_metrics.description: If students have strong fears, they may ask not to be called on; respect the particular student’s wishes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accommodate reasonable requests while maintaining equitable participation overall.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide institutional guidelines on examinations and cheating
rubrics_metrics.description: To provide instructors with a statement of institutional guidelines regarding examinations and cheating.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gather and distribute official policies; ensure instructors understand formal procedures and contacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarify instructor responsibilities for exams and proctoring
rubrics_metrics.description: To provide instructors with a clear idea of what they are expected to do when they give and proctor examinations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outline duties such as active proctoring, attendance records, search procedures, and appropriate interventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarify procedures when cheating is suspected
rubrics_metrics.description: To provide instructors with a clear idea of what they should do if they suspect that students are attempting to cheat on the exam.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize following institutional procedures, documenting observations, and avoiding unofficial punitive actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide ideas for returning graded exam papers
rubrics_metrics.description: To provide instructors with ideas for how and when to return graded exam papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss pros and cons of returning exams in class vs. office pickup, posting statistics, and policies to prevent tampering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide forum for questions about exam processes
rubrics_metrics.description: To provide instructors with a forum to have their questions about the examination process answered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow time in the meeting for Q&A and examples from experienced proctors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gather institutional/departmental exam guidelines before meeting
rubrics_metrics.description: Gather institutional or departmental guidelines on examinations and cheating, if any such guidelines exist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bring printed copies to the meeting so participants can review and discuss specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review and adapt proctoring handout to institutional norms
rubrics_metrics.description: Review and modify the handout on examinations and proctoring to bring it into line with the standards and customs of your institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Customize examples, forms, and contact information to local policies and procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Circulate meeting agenda in advance
rubrics_metrics.description: Circulate the agenda for the meeting to all participants well in advance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advance notice allows participants to prepare questions and bring relevant materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare copies of proctoring materials and confirm attendance
rubrics_metrics.description: Make copies of meeting materials and any questionnaires to distribute, and confirm attendance with participants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure logistical preparedness so the short meeting can run smoothly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agenda should include regulations, responsibilities, cheating responses, and return methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Agenda items: (1) Outline departmental/institutional regulations on exams and cheating, (2) Statement of instructor responsibilities, (3) Discussion of what to do if you suspect cheating, (4) Discussion of methods for returning graded papers and preventing alteration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure the meeting to cover procedural knowledge and practical tactics for consistent implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow a timed meeting outline focused on handout review and Q&A
rubrics_metrics.description: Suggested timing: introduce and review agenda; distribute modified handout and highlight proctoring sections; focus on cheating procedures; review returning papers; wrap up with summary and questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep meeting short (≈30 minutes) and businesslike; use experienced instructors' anecdotes for concreteness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare copies of institutional guidelines and proctoring handout
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare meeting materials: copies of institutional/departmental guidelines and the handout 'Proctoring Tests and Examinations.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make these readily available so instructors can reference official procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize common cheating behaviors
rubrics_metrics.description: On uniform exams, worrying behaviors include: looking at other people's work; showing work to other students (or allowing others to see work); using materials or references not permitted on the exam (inside and outside the exam room).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be familiar with common cheating signs so proctors can discriminate suspicious from innocuous behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: If you observe cheating, tell co-proctor and follow institutional procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: If you observe behavior that you consider to be cheating and you share the exam room with another instructor, tell them what you have seen. Remember that your institution will have established procedures for dealing with academic dishonesty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document observations and seating to support later comparisons; do not apply 'home-made' justice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be certain before taking action against suspected cheating
rubrics_metrics.description: Many innocent behaviors may look like cheating; please be absolutely certain that cheating has or is occurring before taking any action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Err on the side of careful observation and documentation; avoid punitive immediate responses without evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevent cheating through good active proctoring
rubrics_metrics.description: An ounce of prevention is worth (at least) a pound of cure; perhaps the best way of preventing cheating is through good proctoring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Active movement, attentiveness, and clear presence reduce cheating opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not bring reading or amusements; proctor actively and circulate
rubrics_metrics.description: While students are taking the exam, it is important for you to proctor actively. Do not bring reading material or other amusements; proctors should move around the room, keeping tabs on what is happening.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signal attention through movement and posture; avoid giving impression of inattention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make eye contact with students whose behavior is suspicious
rubrics_metrics.description: One trick is to make (and briefly sustain) eye contact with any person whose behavior is making you nervous or suspicious.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eye contact is a low-key cue that can deter dishonest behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep a definitive list of students present and use it to check exams
rubrics_metrics.description: Make a list of the students from your class who are in the exam room; at the end of the exam use it to check off exams as you receive them to be sure everyone handed in their exam.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attendance list helps resolve later disputes about presence or missing papers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search the room before leaving (wastebaskets, under desks/chairs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Before leaving the exam room, make a thorough search of the room, including waste-paper baskets, under desks and chairs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Search can find unsubmitted exams or hidden materials; be systematic but discreet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handle exams from students not in your class appropriately
rubrics_metrics.description: If a student who is not in your class wants to hand you their paper, either pass it immediately to the appropriate instructor or refuse to accept it and insist the student hand it to their own instructor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid confusion across multiple classes sharing a room; ensure papers go to correct instructor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitor bathroom/exit requests; insist on escort if absences are long or repeated
rubrics_metrics.description: If a student is gone for a long time, or asks to leave the room repeatedly, then it is probably time to get suspicious, and perhaps time to insist on an escort.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manage movement during exams to limit opportunities for cheating; know location of nearest bathroom.

rubrics_metrics.name: Carefully consider whether to review exams in class
rubrics_metrics.description: When returning papers to students, it is important for students to understand what mistakes they made, but spending an entire class period going over the exam can be futile and disruptive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weigh disruption risk against pedagogical value; consider targeted review strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: If returning exams in class, do so at the end of class and consider posting statistics
rubrics_metrics.description: If you decide to return graded exams in class, it may be least disruptive to return the exams at the end of the class period. Some instructors post class mean or median as an overall indicator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Posting class statistics can boost morale or provoke concern; plan communication carefully.

rubrics_metrics.name: Announce 'no changes if exam leaves room' policy to prevent tampering
rubrics_metrics.description: Some instructors announce an 'If the exam leaves the room, I can’t make any changes to the score' policy before returning papers to students.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A clear policy discourages post-return tampering; enforce consistently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offer office-hour pickup as alternative to in-class return
rubrics_metrics.description: Alternative approach: have students come to office hours or make short appointments to pick up exams, enabling private discussion and preventing alteration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advantages include private grade discussions, targeted feedback, and reduced opportunity for tampering; requires instructor time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not discuss specific individuals' performance in front of others
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not discuss with students how specific individuals performed on the exam; descriptive statistics should be enough.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protect student privacy and maintain professionalism; avoid naming or ranking students publicly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not name students when discussing grades with colleagues
rubrics_metrics.description: If you discuss grades with other instructors, please do not name names.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preserve confidentiality and collegiality when discussing student performance across instructors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not discuss perceptions of a student's ability publicly
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not discuss your perception of a student’s ability in front of other students, whether from your own class or another class.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Private performance conversations should be respectful and confidential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not re-grade exams in front of students
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not re-grade exams in front of students.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Handle re-grade requests privately to avoid setting inconsistent standards publicly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid in-class debates over grading fairness
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not get into debates over grading policies, or the fairness of exam questions; point out that everyone took the same exam and grading scheme was applied to everyone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defer substantive disputes to private meetings or formal review channels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require written statements for re-grade requests
rubrics_metrics.description: If students insist on having their exam re-graded, ask them to write a statement explaining why they deserve more credit; evaluate their request based on this statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Written explanations help distinguish genuine errors from grade-grubbing and provide documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain consistent grading standards across the class
rubrics_metrics.description: All of the exams in your class ought to have been graded to the same standard, and re-grading individual exams to a different standard upsets this.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply rubrics and norms consistently; be transparent about criteria to reduce disputes.
